citations.assessment: The midrash gives Berekhya son of Ḥelbo citing Abba Samukid about the elders in Joshua.
The commentary explicitly says Samukid is his name.
The opening halakhah gives Berekhya and Ḥelbo jointly in the name of R. Abba Samuka. Its subject is the distance across the creatures’ hooves, a different teaching from the midrash.

evidence.witness: The Jerusalem Talmud, edition by Heinrich W. Guggenheimer. Berlin, De Gruyter, 1999-2015

holds.reason: Both forms and both transmission chains are attested in the checked sources, in different teachings. Preserve the conjecture without adopting a single form.
